newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - May 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - May 14.

text.p: These are significant items in the Ivorian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these items and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Ivory Coast says companies should not be afraid of registering for a national census. So far only 1,600 out of 8,000 companies are registered. Others are afraid they will be pursued by tax authorities.
- President Henri Konan Bedie, on an official visit to Singapore, says it is a model for Ivorian development.

- Secondary school teachers' union does not show up for a meeting with the education minister to discuss a five-day strike. The teachers have decided to stay on strike until Friday, as they had planned.
- Ivory Coast's informal sector contributes around 10 billion CFA every year to government and amounts to 17 percent of the national economy, a study by the National Institute of Statistics says.
- West African Development Bank (BOAD) puts its emphasis in Ivory Coast on financing the private sector, says its country director Babacar Faye.
